votes.motion: Approve the Formal meeting minutes of July 12, 2022 as well as the Living Traditions luncheon minutes of May 17, 2022.
votes.description: Approves the official minutes from the July 12, 2022 Formal Meeting and the May 17, 2022 Living Traditions luncheon.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 22 of 2022, a joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall recognizing September as National Suicide Prevention and Action Month.
votes.description: A ceremonial resolution jointly adopted with the Mayor to designate September as National Suicide Prevention and Action Month in Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and partially adopt Ordinance 44 of 2022, amending the Fiscal Year 2023 final budget of Salt Lake City including the employment staffing document only for items A-4 (GO Bond Public Outreach and Engagement, $150,000 from General Fund Balance) and D-2 (CIP Transfer for General Fund Security, $1,200,000 from CIP Fund to General Fund).
votes.description: Partially adopts Budget Amendment No. 1 for FY2023, approving specific line items for GO Bond public outreach funding and a CIP security transfer while closing the public hearing.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Item B-2 (2022 Train the Trainer Education Grant – Workday Human Resource Management Software) to a future Consent Agenda for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on a grant application from the Finance Department for Workday software training and refers it to a future consent agenda for formal approval.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 45 of 2022, amending the zoning of the property at approximately 1902 North, 1932 North, 1944 North, and 1954 North Rose Park Lane from R-1/7,000 (Single Family Residential District) to OS (Open Space District).
votes.description: Rezones four parcels on Rose Park Lane to Open Space to allow their incorporation into the Regional Athletic Complex, also amending the Rose Park Small Area Plan Future Land Use Map.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 46 of 2022, amending the zoning of the property located at approximately 858 West and 860 West Hoyt Place from R-1/5,000 (Single Family Residential District) to SR-3 (Special Development Pattern Residential District).
votes.description: Rezones two lots on Hoyt Place to SR-3 to allow subdivision and construction of two additional single-family homes at the rear of the property while retaining two existing renovated homes.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 47 of 2022, amending the zoning of the property located at approximately 805 South 800 West from M-1 (Light Manufacturing District) to R-MU-35 (Residential/Mixed Use District).
votes.description: Rezones a property at 805 South 800 West from light manufacturing to residential/mixed use to accommodate a potential multi-family or attached single-family development.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 48 of 2022, amending the general plan land use designation of a property located at approximately 2435 South 500 East from Low Density Residential to Medium Density Residential and the zoning map from R-1-7,000 Residential to RMF-35 Moderate Density Multi-Family Residential District.
votes.description: Amends both the master plan and zoning map for a property at 2435 South 500 East to facilitate construction of townhomes by allowing higher-density residential use.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 49 of 2022, amending the zoning text of Subsection 21A.24.110.F of the Salt Lake City Code pertaining to building coverage in the R-2 Single and Two-Family Residential District.
votes.description: Increases the allowable building coverage for single-family homes in the R-2 district from 40% to 45% city-wide to align with the existing 45% limit for duplexes.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 23 of 2022, adopting the Capital Improvement Program project-specific allocations for Fiscal Year 2023 as shown on the attached Exhibit A Funding Log.
votes.description: Approves specific project funding allocations for the City's Capital Improvement Program for FY2023, covering construction, renovation, and purchase of city-owned physical structures.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 50 of 2022, amending the Salt Lake City Code Chapter 2.20 to modify the membership of the Community Recovery Committee.
votes.description: Amends city code to update the membership structure of the Community Recovery Committee, which oversees distribution of American Rescue Plan Act funds.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 51 of 2022, granting a Telecommunication Franchise to Uniti National, LLC.
votes.description: Grants a new telecommunications franchise agreement to Uniti National, LLC, allowing the company to place and maintain facilities within City rights-of-way subject to permits and applicable taxes.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 24 of 2022, providing for the holding of a local special bond election for $80 million General Obligation Bonds for parks, trails and open space, with a public hearing on October 11 and a public meeting on October 18, and encouraging the Administration to seek funding from external sources for any project receiving bond funding.
votes.description: Places an $80 million General Obligation Bond measure on the ballot for voters to decide on financing capital improvements to city-owned parks, trails, open space, and related recreational facilities.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 25 of 2022, authorizing up to $67.5 million of sales and excise tax revenue bonds; giving authority to certain officers to approve the final terms and provisions of the bonds within specified parameters; adding 'irrigation' to the City Cemetery road repairs and reconstruction project; and encouraging the Administration to seek funding from external sources for any project receiving bond funding.
votes.description: Authorizes issuance of up to $67.5 million in sales and excise tax revenue bonds to finance capital improvement projects including historic properties and critical infrastructure upgrades.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 52 of 2022 approving a $350,000 loan for Chip Cookies, LLC, from the Economic Development Loan Fund.
votes.description: Approves a $350,000 EDLF loan to Chip Cookies, LLC to support expansion of their production and administrative operations at 4752 W California Ave.

votes.motion: Approve the Consent Agenda with a modification to Item G-2 for the Airport Master Plan, to add a public hearing date of October 18 and adjust the timeline for action to – To Be Determined following the public hearings.
votes.description: Approves all consent agenda items including setting public hearing dates for two items, approving seven Community Recovery Committee board appointments, and modifying the Airport Master Plan timeline.
